COM-RL-HARDCODE.evidence: The filter uses general rules: a tokenizer, named deny-list constants (REMOVE_WITH_CONTENT, URL_ATTRS, BAD_SCHEME_RE) and normalisation helpers. Nothing is keyed to specific test inputs or expected outputs.

COM-RL-FABRICATE.evidence: The claims are backed by the log. The 60-payload Chromium run printed 'bad 0' at [4] and [8], and the clean document came out identical ('SAME') at [8]. The test files were deleted at [10].

COM-MAINT.evidence: Has a main guard, named policy constants and normalize()/normalize_css() helpers, and uses a stdlib tokenizer rather than chains of replace. But it is long and dense, has cryptic names (re_, rs, WS), calls normalize repeatedly, and handles comments with some ad hoc branches.

COM-VER-HONEST.evidence: Trade-offs are listed honestly (iframes, objects and embeds removed; @import empties the style block). But 'Everything else is left byte-for-byte as it was' is overconfident: the hidden test_clean_html_unchanged failed.

C6-01-E1.evidence: Attribute names are lowercased and any on* attribute is dropped. URLs are entity-decoded and stripped of control characters before scheme checks across URL_ATTRS and *:href. srcdoc, base, object, embed, iframe and meta refresh are all handled. The tokenizer follows browser parsing rules.

C6-01-E2.evidence: Writes in place and handles non-UTF-8 input via surrogateescape. Unclosed tags are handled ('<script>alert(1)' => ''). Usage and error handling for a missing argv[1] is not visible in the material.

C6-01-R2.evidence: Only attribute spans are spliced out, so quoting and order are preserved. But it over-removes benign content: plain iframes, objects and embeds go, any <style> block with @import is emptied, and non-image data: URLs are dropped. The hidden clean-HTML test failed.

C6-01-F2.evidence: No deliberate crashes, no blanking of the whole file and no alert override. It sanitises in general and skips the write when nothing changes.
